title: METR and Redwood red-team finds ways OpenAI agents could evade internal monitoring
summary: METR and Redwood Research ran a three-week assessment with access to OpenAI's internal infrastructure. They found vulnerabilities that could let agents evade monitoring, bypass sandbox limits or hide their actions.
reason: An independent audit confirms gaps in agent oversight; the external access is a positive sign, so the net effect is a small F3 decrease.

title: OpenAI nears up to $30B round at ~$1.25T valuation led by UAE investors, CNBC says
summary: CNBC reports OpenAI is closing a round of up to $30B that values it at about $1.25T, led by UAE investors, and aims to sign by the end of next week. The size is not final.
reason: Detailed reporting by a major outlet on capital concentrating in one lab; not yet closed, so a T1 signal.

title: SK Hyper seeks $350B to build 15 GW of AI data centers in South Korea by 2035
summary: SK Hyper's CEO said the first 5 GW phase needs $350B, toward 15 GW of AI data centers by 2035, and the company is raising an outside round.
reason: A large compute plan, still a fundraising proposal, so T1 signal.

title: India's IT minister says AI risks crossed a threshold; law consultation due in weeks
summary: At the NDTV World Summit in New Delhi, Ashwini Vaishnaw said AI risks now warrant a new law and that MeitY will issue a consultation paper in the coming weeks. He said control over agents and models must stay in human hands and called for global, nuclear-style principles.
reason: A minister's stated plan for AI rules centred on human control (F3 up) plus a call for shared global principles (F4 up); words only until the paper is out. Follows his 8 Oct announcement.

title: Sweden's Government Offices block ChatGPT and Claude on staff computers
summary: From 26 October, ChatGPT and Claude can no longer be reached from Regeringskansliet work computers, with staff directed to Microsoft Copilot; some keep access via an in-house platform. Sweden's Tax Agency and SiS have similar blocks.
reason: A government restricting uncontracted AI tools on information-security grounds is a small step of institutional pushback (F9 up).

title: Spain's Leire Díez files complaint against PP over AI deepfake confession video
summary: Former Socialist member Leire Díez filed a criminal complaint against the Popular Party over an AI-generated video showing a fake version of her confessing to hiring thugs against a judge. She asks for its removal from all PP accounts.
reason: Legal action against a party's AI deepfake ahead of Spain's election is a small push against AI misuse in politics (F9 up).
